sections.label: Ocean plastic pollution study
sections.summary: A study found 1.8 trillion pieces of plastic floating between California and Hawaii, and researchers estimate eight million tonnes are dumped yearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: A recent study found 1.8 trillion pieces of plastic, weighing a total of 80,000 tonnes, currently floating in a stretch of ocean between California and Hawaii.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And researchers estimate that humans dump eight million tonnes of plastic in the ocean every year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If we do not do anything about it, there will be more plastic than fish in our ocean by 2050.

sections.label: Singapore plastic bag discards 2016
sections.summary: In 2016, Singapore discarded 27 billion plastic bags, averaging 13 bags per person per day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In 2016, Singapore discarded 27 billion plastic bags, an average of 13 bags per person per day.

sections.label: Mandatory packaging reporting plans
sections.summary: Businesses will soon be mandated to report the type and amount of packaging they put on the market and their reduction plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Soon, we will mandate businesses to report on the type and amount of packaging they put on the market and their plans for reduction.

sections.label: Miniso plastic bag charge results
sections.summary: After a 10-cent plastic bag charge in 2017, Miniso reported a 75% drop in customers' plastic bag usage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: After implementing a 10-cent plastic bag charge in 2017, lifestyle brand Miniso reported that customers’ plastic bag usage dropped by 75%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In 2007, they implemented a 10-cent plastic bag charge; in 2013, they stopped offering disposable bags entirely.

sections.label: Yi Hong Minimart plastic bag cost
sections.summary: Yi Hong Minimart spends $2,000 to $3,000 on plastic bags each month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Yi Hong Minimart spends $2,000 to $3,000 on plastic bags each month, or one month alone.

sections.label: Questions on plastic waste reduction
sections.summary: Four questions ask about public sector plastic waste reduction, single-use plastic at events, NDP 2019 items, and carrier bag charges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One, will we be putting more emphasis on plastic waste reduction in our public sector's sustainability plan?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Two, will the Public Service be eliminating single-use plastic from their catering events?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Three, will NDP 2019 use only reusable items with minimal packaging?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Lastly, and four, will the Government implement a charge for single-use carrier bags of all materials and not just plastic bags?

sections.label: Packaging share of domestic waste
sections.summary: One third of domestic waste comes from packaging.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: One third of domestic waste comes from packaging.

sections.label: Singapore Packaging Agreement and reporting
sections.summary: The 2007 Singapore Packaging Agreement cut some 46,000 tonnes of packaging, and reporting requirements were brought forward to 2020 under a regulatory system.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: We started the Singapore Packaging Agreement in 2007.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: This voluntary initiative is well-supported by companies and has collectively reduced some 46,000 tonnes of packaging.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: We are now moving to a regulatory system to tackle packaging waste systematically on a large scale.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Hence, we brought forward the requirement for businesses to report the type and amount of packaging they are putting on the market and their plans for reduction, by one year, to 2020.

sections.label: Singapore marine plastic pollution ranking
sections.summary: Studies including a 2015 University of Georgia study and a 2016 UN Environment report acknowledge Singapore as one of the smallest contributors to marine plastic pollution.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The result is that Singapore is acknowledged as one of the smallest contributors to marine plastic pollution in the world, according to studies, including a 2015 University of Georgia study on "Plastic Waste Inputs from Land into the Ocean" and the UN Environment’s 2016 report on marine plastic debris and microplastics.

sections.label: Bring-Your-Own Campaign results
sections.summary: NEA supported Zero Waste SG's Bring-Your-Own Campaign, which involved 430 retailers and F&B companies and averted two million pieces of plastic disposables.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Last year, NEA supported Zero Waste SG’s Bring-Your-Own Campaign that brought 430 retailers and food and beverage (F&B) companies together to incentivise consumers to bring their own reusable containers and bags.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Not only did it raise awareness, it also averted the use of two million pieces of plastic disposables.

sections.label: Enforcement and plastic bag reuse
sections.summary: Enforcement is complicated, Hong Kong's non-compliance rate is about a third to half, and a survey showed two-thirds of respondents reuse plastic bags for waste.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: But as he also noted, this complicates the system, making enforcement even more difficult.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: I understand from reports, as Mr Louis Ng also pointed out, that the non-compliance rate in Hong Kong is about a third to half.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The Singapore Environment Council's latest survey showed that two-thirds of respondents use their plastic bags for bagging waste.

sections.label: Study on single-use disposables
sections.summary: An extensive study on single-use carrier bags and disposables showed other disposables do not necessarily give better environmental outcomes, and a British study found 173 uses needed for reusable tote bags.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: With regard to the study, actually we have already done an extensive study on single-use carrier bags and disposables, and we have shared in this House and with the Member, too, the results of the study where it showed it is not necessarily true that using other types of disposables versus plastics will give you a better environmental outcome or impact.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: As I also noted earlier in this speech, even the British study has shown that for a reusable tote bag to benefit in terms of greenhouse gas emission reduction, you have to use it 173 times.

sections.label: Waste and environment regulatory measures
sections.summary: The passage states regulatory measures will be implemented to manage waste and protect the environment, including carbon tax, e-waste EPR, and mandatory packaging waste reporting and reduction plans.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: And we will not hesitate to implement and take regulatory measures to manage waste and to protect the environment where we think it is practicable, effective and useful to do so.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: So, we will be implementing carbon tax, as well as EPR on e-waste, as well as mandatory reporting for packaging waste and the reduction plans.

sections.label: NDP 2030 decision timing
sections.summary: The passage states the decision on NDP 2030 will be left to whoever is Minister for the Environment and Water Resources at that point in time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: Senior Minister of State, you have only one and a half minutes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: We will leave it to whoever the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources is at that point in time to decide on NDP 2030.
